title: Songs in Indian Popular Cinema
objective: After this level you can explain why popular Hindi films weave song and dance into their stories and use playback singers.
summary: India's first talkie, Alam Ara (1931), was full of songs. Popular Hindi films inherited song from Parsi theatre, use it in every genre, and rely on playback singers.

cards.headline: In 1931, India's first talking picture was also a singing one.
cards.body: Alam Ara, India's first talkie, was advertised as 'All talking, all singing, all dancing' and packed in seven song sequences. Songs are still at the heart of popular Hindi films, whatever their genre. Why do these stories stop for a song, and who is really singing?

cards.headline: The songs came before the cinema
cards.body: Hindi film didn't invent the song-filled story. Parsi theatre, which flourished from the 1850s to the 1930s, combined folk and musical theatre traditions and was a forerunner of Bollywood, the Hindi film industry named from Bombay plus Hollywood. When sound reached Indian cinema in 1931, the screen could finally sing too.

cards.headline: Not a genre, an ingredient
cards.body: In Hollywood, the musical is one genre among many. In Bollywood, song and dance turn up in all the others, from family dramas to action films. They're good business, too: Britannica notes that soundtracks and choreographed set pieces are often the engines that drive a film's box office. A hit song sells the ticket.

cards.headline: The voice behind the star
cards.body: Here's the twist: the star on screen usually isn't the one singing. Playback singers prerecord the songs, and the actors lip-sync to them; the singers never appear. The greatest became legends anyway. Lata Mangeshkar recorded songs for more than 2,000 Indian films. One voice, many faces.

questions.prompt: In most popular Hindi films, the songs are actually sung by _____.

options.label: a choir behind the actors
options.rationale: The singers never appear on screen.

questions.explanation: Playback singers prerecord the songs, and the actors lip-sync on screen.

questions.prompt: Why are songs so central to popular Hindi films?

options.label: Indian law has required at least seven songs in every film since 1931
options.rationale: Alam Ara had seven, but no law requires them.

options.label: They grew from song-filled Parsi theatre, and hit songs help drive box office
Hindi films are all musicals, so the industry has no other genres
options.rationale: Song runs through many genres; it is not one genre.

options.label: Songs replaced spoken dialogue in Hindi films until the 1970s
options.rationale: Alam Ara was all talking as well as singing.

questions.explanation: Parsi theatre was a musical forerunner of Bollywood, and soundtracks and set pieces often drive box office.

questions.prompt: Playback singing only works if lips match a recorded voice. What did Level 3 say sound films did to keep voices in sync?

options.label: Cranked cameras faster by hand
options.rationale: Hand cranks wobble; that's the problem sound solved.

options.label: Ran cameras at an even, motorized 24 frames per second
Showed each frame twice with a twin-bladed shutter

questions.explanation: Sound fixed the speed at 24 frames per second, and motorized cameras kept voices in step with moving lips.
